_comment: TEMPLATE — do not copy this file into place by hand. Install it with `bash tools/install-hooks.sh`, which substitutes __REPO_ROOT__ for the real container root and MERGES these entries into the target settings file instead of overwriting it. Every entry is tagged 'portfolio-checkpoint-hooks'; the installer only ever replaces entries carrying that tag, so a user's own permissions, env and other projects' hooks survive. WHY NOT THIS REPO'S OWN .claude/settings.json: confirmed 2026-09-10 that Claude Code on the web does not load hooks from a repo that sits in a subdirectory of the session root — CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is unset and one project root is resolved for the whole session. The commands below glob every repo under that root, so one install protects every project in the container, and each entry point aggregates all repos into ONE JSON object (see tools/hooks/emit.py — two objects do not parse, and that silently cost the entire session briefing).

hooks.command: for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/brief.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # portfolio-checkpoint-hooks
hooks.statusMessage: Reading where the last session stopped...
